editorial_note: Original writing informed by community discussions about both recognisable traits and tired stereotypes. These are creative sign-level lines, not personal natal-chart readings.

one_liners: Not distant. Just thinking three timelines ahead.
I left the group chat mentally before anyone noticed.
Normal was never a serious option.
I have feelings. They are currently in peer review.
The niche interest is becoming a presentation. Clear your evening.
Socially present, spiritually in airplane mode.
I questioned the rule and accidentally redesigned the system.
Too original for the template, too stubborn for the trend.
I care about humanity. Individual humans require scheduling.
My weird phase has excellent long-term prospects.
I am emotionally available in an unconventional file format.
The future texted. I left it on read to think.
I did it before it was cool and after it became useful.
My rebellion has a spreadsheet and community guidelines.
I need people in theory and alone time in practice.
Detached is a strong word for internally processing at satellite speed.
The rule made sense until I looked at it.
I brought a strange idea and enough facts to make it inconvenient.
My social circle is curated like an obscure playlist.
I refuse the box, then organise everyone outside it.
affirmations_predictions: The idea that feels too strange for the room may be the one worth keeping.
A friendship deepens when you trade clever distance for one honest sentence.
Your future gets clearer when you build with people, not only for them.
An unexpected collaborator understands the vision faster than expected.
You can belong to the group without surrendering your edges.
A private feeling becomes easier once you give it ordinary words.
Your refusal to copy the obvious answer creates a better one.
A community you nearly overlooked will make room for your full self.
An unusual solution earns support once you show how it helps real people.
A friendship becomes warmer when analysis makes room for affection.
You will find your people in a smaller, stranger corner than expected.
The future you imagine needs one boring system to survive.
A group project works when you share ownership, not only ideas.
Someone understands your need for space without reading it as rejection.
Your originality becomes practical at exactly the right moment.
A cause matters more when you let individual stories reach you.
You are ready to update an identity that once kept you independent.
The next breakthrough comes from revisiting an old rule with new evidence.
A surprising invitation pulls you out of observer mode.
Your difference stops feeling lonely when it becomes useful to a community.
micro_poems: you call it worth a try.
you love the whole wide future,
each time you let it break.
